name: ccdebugger-native
experiment:
# Real CC-Debugger + CC2530 through the NATIVE USB backend (no cc-tool).
#
# This RESETS the target into debug halt (access: reset-debug-session), reads
# status, registers and 16 bytes of CODE and physical flash, then re-enables DMA
# and resumes the firmware. It never writes memory, erases or programs flash.
#
#   make build && ./bin/hwlab run --yes examples/ccdebugger-native.yaml
name: ccdebugger-native
duration: 2s

devices:
  dbg:
    plugin: ccdebugger
    backend: native
    access: reset-debug-session
    allow_target_reset: true
    allow_cpu_control: true
    allow_memory_access: true
    allow_dma_enable: true

steps:
  - {name: identify, at: 100ms, device: dbg, call: DebugProbe.info}
  - {name: attach, at: 200ms, device: dbg, call: DebugProbe.attach}
  - {name: status, at: 300ms, device: dbg, call: DebugProbe.status}
  - {name: registers, at: 400ms, device: dbg, call: DebugProbe.read_registers}
  - {name: code, at: 500ms, device: dbg, call: MemoryAccess.read, args: {space: code, address: 0, length: 16}}
  - {name: flash, at: 600ms, device: dbg, call: MemoryAccess.read, args: {space: flash, address: 0x8000, length: 16}}
  - {name: dma, at: 700ms, device: dbg, call: DebugProbe.enable_dma}
  - {name: run, at: 800ms, device: dbg, call: DebugProbe.resume}
